headline: Western Europe sets temperature record as heat waves hit
summary: June and July averaged a record 21.62°C across Western Europe, with drought, wildfires and low rivers adding pressure.
script: Western Europe has set a new temperature record. June and July averaged twenty-one point six two degrees Celsius, while heat waves drove drought, wildfires and dangerously low rivers across the region.
imageAlt: People walk on a newly exposed sandbar beneath Budapest’s Margareth Bridge.
imageAltTwo: A second view of the exposed Danube riverbed during Europe’s heat and drought.
